title: Edward Jenner's smallpox vaccination
summary: On 14 May 1796 in Berkeley, Gloucestershire, Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with matter from the cowpox lesions of the dairymaid Sarah Nelms. When he inoculated the boy again in July with matter from a fresh smallpox lesion, no disease developed, and Jenner concluded the protection was complete. The World Health Organization dates the world's first vaccine demonstration to this experiment and records its declaring smallpox eradicated in 1980.

uncertainty.note: Jenner inoculated James Phipps with cowpox on 14 May 1796 and tested immunity with variolation in July 1796.

as_recorded.value: On May 14, 1796, using matter from Nelms' lesions, he inoculated an 8-year-old boy, James Phipps
It wasn’t until May 1796 that the world’s first vaccine was demonstrated

where.historical_name: Berkeley, Gloucestershire, Kingdom of Great Britain

importance.justification: Jenner's work is widely regarded as the foundation of immunology (Baylor University Medical Center Proceedings), and the World Health Organization records smallpox, the only human disease eradicated so far, as eradicated in 1980.

related.because: Jenner's demonstration of cowpox vaccination began the global vaccination efforts that ultimately eradicated smallpox in 1980.

beats.caption: In Berkeley, Edward Jenner inoculates James Phipps with cowpox matter taken from a lesion on milkmaid Sarah Nelmes.
Challenged with smallpox matter, Phipps develops no disease, proving that cowpox inoculation confers immunity against smallpox.
